tested:
NPX-137 (2026-09-12): a real IOL L3 binary imported and registered as
"tpgen-adventerprisek9-124" (the vendor-image DIRECTORY name was used as the
registry `name`, not the actual binary filename inside it,
`i86bi-linux-l3-tpgen-adventerprisek9-12.4.bin`) - the same class of "bare-named
IOL build" this section's "l2-adventerprisek9"/"l3-adventerprisek9" entries already
exist for, just with a "tpgen-" prefix neither of those two keys' prefix/substring
matching covers. Without this entry, `_match_profile_key`/`_match_data_iface_key`
both silently fail to recognize this image as IOL at all, and
`data_interface_name()` falls all the way back to the generic-Linux "eth0" instead
of this platform's real "Ethernet0/0" - live-reproduced: boot_verify.py's
dataplane-verify stage sent a real "no shutdown" to a data-plane interface named
"eth0" that does not exist on this device, so the real interface stayed
administratively down and the check correctly (if unhelpfully) reported zero
frames forwarded, even though the image itself boots and takes console commands
completely normally (confirmed via a direct single-node reproduction).

reasons.min_ram_mb:
default_ram_mb 512 -> 1024 (NPX-1527 PROFILES-TOOLS pass-3, rule #59): EVE-NG's
real iol.yml sets ram: 1024 with no separate default/floor split - the old 512
here had no written reason, matching EVE exactly now.
reasons.nic: NPX-1527 review (Wave 38): IolProvider.get_console returns ConsoleType.SERIAL (raw PTY bridge), so the profile must say "serial" - not EVE's "telnet" label; verified in iol_provider.py get_console. No consumer treats the two differently today.

settings.description: Cisco IOL L3 router (bare-named build, tpgen- vendor-directory naming) - requires 32-bit userspace libc.
